summary.headline: Laxmi India Finance Q1 FY27 PAT rose ~70% YoY to INR16.4 crore, NIM expanded to 11.36%, while credit cost jumped to 0.95% on vehicle loans.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 showed strong growth: AUM up 28% YoY to INR1,721.7 crore, own book up 31.7% to INR1,626.9 crore, and disbursements of INR232 crore versus INR166 crore a year ago. Profitability improved sharply, with PBT up ~72% to INR21.9 crore and PAT up ~70% to INR16.4 crore, driven by a 67 bps fall in cost of borrowing to 10.66%. Asset quality improved sequentially (GNPA 2.08%, NNPA 0.93%), but credit cost rose to INR3.69 crore (0.95%) from 0.58%, attributed mainly to vehicle finance and an extra 10% provisioning on up-money cases. Management kept FY27 PAT growth guidance of 40-45% and AUM growth of 30-35% unchanged.

segments.name: MSME (secured SME)
segments.commentary: Core vertical at ~INR1,395 crore AUM; management says core MSME and construction credit costs remain moderate. A new prime MSME product for INR25-50 lakh tickets was recently launched.

segments.commentary: AUM ~INR131 crore; source of the credit cost rise, attributed to older vintages in specific geographies. Acceptance criteria tightened and field follow-ups increased.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth target of ~30-35% annually maintained.
FY27 PAT growth guidance of ~40-45% maintained; Q1 PAT growth stated to be significantly ahead of this range, with revision to be considered after the next few quarters.
Targeted ROA of 3.5-3.75% by year-end, per analyst question and management reply.
Further 20-25 bps reduction in cost of borrowing expected over coming quarters, assuming stable global rates and no RBI hike.
Cost-to-income ratio currently below 50%; internal target ~42-44%.
Plan to add 30-35 branches across existing states in FY27; 10 added in Q1. One or two new states planned per year.
Capital raise of ~INR300-350 crore planned in roughly 1-1.5 years (start of next financial year), when leverage reaches ~3.5-4x (pre-IPO level ~4-4.5x).
capex_capacity: Branch network at 184 across six states (Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra); 25 branches added over the last year, including 10 in UP and 6 in Maharashtra.
New branches reach breakeven in ~7-9 months (range 5-12 months) at an AUM of ~INR1.5-2 crore per branch; one of the 25 new branches is already at breakeven.
Branches are tiered: Tier 1 with 5-6 relationship officers, Tier 2 with 5-6, Tier 3 with 2-5.
Rajasthan (mother state, ~90 branches) remains the largest contributor; other states are expected to gain share over 3-4 years.
Digitised LOS/LMS, CKYC, RCU, eNACH and auto-dialer; only physical loan signing remains, expected to move to eSign shortly.
demand_pricing: Disbursements of INR232 crore grew ~40% YoY, ahead of 28% AUM growth; management attributes the gap to repayments and closures.
Portfolio yield broadly stable at 21.67%; NIM gain came from lower funding cost, not yield.
Management said it may pass on borrowing-cost relief to borrowers depending on asset quality and board decision.
37% of borrowers are first-time borrowers; customer base at ~43,946 vs 37,122 a year ago.
Management flagged rising competitive intensity in MSME lending and said underwriting discipline will be maintained.

qa_highlights.question: How are the new branches performing versus the mature network, and what is the gestation period to steady-state productivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Of 25 branches opened in the last year, one has reached breakeven. Breakeven takes about 7-9 months (5-12 months range) at branch AUM of roughly INR1.5-2 crore; Tier 1, 2 and 3 branches are staffed with 5-6, 5-6 and 2-5 relationship officers respectively.

qa_highlights.question: Over 3-5 years, what must change to move from a regional NBFC to a pan-India MSME franchise, and what is the biggest constraint?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will enter one or two new states per year, having started in Rajasthan and expanded through Gujarat, MP, Chhattisgarh, UP and Maharashtra. Management said it targets ROA of 3.5-3.75% and expects to reach it by year-end, with current ROA at 3.45%.

qa_highlights.question: What product and geographic mix changes are planned as AUM scales?
qa_highlights.answer: MSME stays the core product, with a new prime MSME product for INR25-50 lakh tickets. Plan is 30-35 branches in existing states in FY27, with 10 added in Q1. Rajasthan (about 90 branches) stays the largest state for the next 3-4 years, with other states gaining share.

qa_highlights.question: Why did credit cost rise to about 1%, and is stress coming from newer geographies or vintages?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to the wheels (vehicle) portfolio, specifically older vintages in certain geographies, and said it is localised. Gopal Krishan Sain said the main P&L driver was an extra 10% provisioning on up-money transactions, with 70% of that provisioning booked so far.

qa_highlights.question: How much balance sheet capacity remains before equity is needed, given CRAR moderation from about 26% to 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt to equity is 2.57x with liquidity of about INR255.9 crore. Management plans to raise about INR300-350 crore in roughly 1-1.5 years, starting next financial year, when leverage reaches about 3.5-4x (pre-IPO about 4-4.5x).

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 and FY28 growth and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: AUM growth of 30-35% CAGR will be maintained. Margins depend on cost of borrowing and yield; management expects to pass some borrowing-cost relief to borrowers once cost of borrowing is in a declining phase.

qa_highlights.question: Are the El Nino and global uncertainties affecting the portfolio, and is AUM being expanded aggressively?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said global conflict has limited direct impact since customers are in Tier 2/3 cities, though crude prices raise borrower costs. It said growth is risk-based, with funding stopped or LTV reduced where stress is seen, and collection efficiency is expected to be maintained.

qa_highlights.question: What were the net slippages in the quarter?
How much further can cost of borrowing fall, what is the sustainable NIM, and where can cost-to-income settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Piyush Somani said another 20-25 bps reduction is expected over coming quarters, assuming stable global rates and no RBI hike; incremental cost of borrowing is about 10.48% over the last 12 months. Cost-to-income is below 50% now, with an internal target of around 42-44%; opex is elevated by new-state branch openings.

qa_highlights.question: How should the gap between 40% disbursement growth and 28% AUM growth be read, and does the run rate support faster AUM growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Kuldeep Singh said the gap reflects repayments and loan closures, and that the current disbursement run rate supports AUM growth.

risks_watch: Vehicle (wheels) finance credit cost: rose to 0.95% of average gross loan (INR3.69 crore) from 0.58%; watch whether the older-vintage stress in specific geographies eases after tighter acceptance criteria and more field follow-ups.
Up-money cases: an extra 10% provisioning is being applied, with 70% of ECL provision booked so far; further provisioning depends on court-led enforcement and collection progress.
Capital: CRAR moderated to 25.32% from about 26%, and a INR300-350 crore raise is planned in roughly 1-1.5 years; execution timing and dilution are open.
Margin sustainability: NIM gain came from funding cost (10.66%, down 67 bps), not yield; management expects only 20-25 bps further cost reduction and may pass some relief to borrowers.
Branch maturity: new branches take 7-9 months on average to breakeven (range 5-12 months); cost-to-income is still above the 42-44% target, and opex grew about 34% YoY.

Competitive intensity in MSME lending is rising; management said underwriting discipline will be maintained. ROA target of 3.5-3.75% and FY27 PAT guidance of 40-45% (Q1 already well ahead) are to be reviewed after the next few quarters.
key_quotes: At the same time, we remain conscious that as we scale, maintaining the quality of our portfolio and discipline our underwriting will remain the most important priority for us.
We believe this is prudent to maintain our existing guidance at this stage and assess the performance over the next few quarters before considering any revision.
We are not looking to grow simply for the sake of balance sheet expansion.
The only manual step remains in our process is physical signing of loan agreements which we expect to move to eSign shortly.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on growth, margins and funding, citing a strong Q1 and keeping FY27 guidance unchanged. It was more cautious on asset quality, particularly vehicle finance, and it gave vague answers on some questions (for example, the exact breakeven AUM per branch and the pass-through of rate cuts).
